reason: Safari can run docs.js before the page's stylesheets apply, so the tag static-multipage's docs.js, which measures the nav's top only when the module runs (and on resize), sometimes measures it in a layout where the nav sits several hundred pixels lower: at each width one of two values, on either side, in 1 to 4% of the docs cells of a run (p2-styles-safari-light-2 and -dark-2, 2026-11-03: 662.1875px or 60.78125px at 1600, 688.75px or 140.015625px at 1300). Chrome and Firefox wait for the stylesheets and never do. dist's docs.js measures again on the window's load since that run, but side A is the frozen tag, so its value still varies in Safari.
notes: tests/README.md, Phase 2, Safari. The behavior check side-menu-max-height holds the formula itself in Chrome and Firefox; the styles gate in those browsers has no such entry.

reason: Safari shows its AutoFill button in a focused field whose autocomplete names AutoFill data (username, email, given-name on these pages), at its own discretion: in a run it shows on one side's field and not the other's, on either side. The field is then exactly 27px wider or narrower (277px against 250px on /docs/version-picker/jade at 375px), and its origins half that (p2-styles-safari-light-2 and -dark-2: 34 records in 17 cells, the Login, Email and First name fields of /docs/color-schemes, /docs/version-picker/jade, /docs/forms/input and /docs/forms).
notes: No WebDriver capability turns AutoFill off, and its setting is the owner's Safari's. Chrome and Firefox add no such button.
